description: We are a team inspired by the Voyager Golden Record, exploring how humanity can communicate its story beyond Earth. Our project focuses on the idea of preserving and sharing human identity through sounds, music, culture, and the things that make us who we are. We aim to bring this concept into a creative space exploration project.
summary:
THE RECEIVER is an interactive 3D WebGL observatory and real-time auditory gateway created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Earth Jukebox). Deeply inspired by NASA’s historic 1977 Voyager mission, our project uses the Golden Record as both its narrative core and live demonstration anchor. In 1977, humanity launched the Golden Record into interstellar space as our outward greeting to the cosmos. THE RECEIVER flips that paradigm: what if an extraterrestrial intelligence intercepted Voyager and tuned their listening arrays back toward Earth today?
 Instead of a static snapshot, the celestial listener hears our living planet across 16 years of environmental telemetry (2010–2026). Our platform bridges 12 NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) planetary datasets—from night lights and CO₂ to sea level rise and wildfires—translating satellite matrices into NASA-IMPACT harmonic MIDI chords, binaural stereo panning, and Chandra binary percussion. Users can explore 27 Voyager musical tracks, listen to 55 language greetings, probe global coordinates via an interactive canvas, and activate our dual-engine audio reader for visually impaired researchers. By uniting Voyager’s legendary heritage with urgent Earth science, THE RECEIVER turns planetary observation into an accessible, living symphony.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

THE RECEIVER is an interactive 3D WebGL observatory and multi-channel sonification suite built with React 19, Three.js, and native Web Audio DSP. It functions as an interstellar receiver tuning into Earth's electromagnetic and environmental emissions across three distinct listening channels:

1. VOYAGER ARCHIVE (1977): Features all 55 historical spoken language greetings, 27 restored traditional and classical musical compositions, and 116 analog-encoded Golden Record images.

2. EARTH SIGNALS (2010–2026): Synthesizes 16 years of time-series planetary telemetry from 12 NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) and GIBS satellite observation datasets.

3. INTERACTIVE WORLD MAP PROBE: An equirectangular canvas scanner where hovering or touching any global coordinate instantly calculates optical density, surface anomalies, and longitude, translating them into dynamic harmonic soundscapes.

Our DSP engine implements the NASA-IMPACT "From Data to Melody" harmonic protocol, mapping optical brightness across 6 octaves of musical frequencies (C1 to A6, 32.7 Hz to 1760 Hz) with binaural stereophonic panning (Western Hemisphere = Left, Eastern Hemisphere = Right). High-energy environmental anomalies (wildfires, super-typhoon eyes, lightning strikes) trigger threshold-activated sub-bass percussion inspired by NASA Chandra X-ray binary sonifications.

2. What benefits does it have?

- Multi-Sensory Data Comprehension: Allows researchers, students, and citizens to hear macroscopic planetary shifts (such as Amazon deforestation or Pacific warming) that are often obscured in static 2D graphs.

- Zero-Installation Web Accessibility: Built entirely on native browser standards (WebGL, Web Audio API), running smoothly across mobile smartphones, tablets, laptops, and 4K displays.

- Inclusive Science: Features a custom Dual-Engine Audio Reader that pairs synthesized voice announcements with 880 Hz pure sine wave acoustic earcons, ensuring that blind and visually impaired users can explore planetary data without relying on screen-reader compatibility alone.

3. What is the intended impact?

By transforming cold numerical satellite measurements into an emotive, living symphony, THE RECEIVER creates visceral empathy for Earth’s delicate biosphere. It bridges NASA’s legendary 20th-century interplanetary exploration (Voyager) with urgent 21st-century climate science, serving as an educational gateway for schools, planetariums, and space enthusiasts worldwide.

4. What tools, coding languages, and software were used?

- Programming Languages: JavaScript (ES2024 / JSX), HTML5 Canvas, WebGL Shader Shading, CSS3.

- Core Frameworks: React 19, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei).

- Audio DSP: W3C Web Audio API (native AudioContext, BiquadFilterNode, StereoPannerNode, OscillatorNode), Tone.js, Web Speech Synthesis API.

- Styling & Interface: Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide React icons, Canvas 2D image processing.

- Version Control: Git, GitHub repository.

5. How is your project creative?

Rather than creating another passive dashboard, THE RECEIVER reframes Earth observation through an imaginative, inverted narrative: humanity is no longer looking out—an alien civilization has caught our 1977 Voyager greeting and is now analyzing the planet that transmitted it. The contrast between the hopeful, pristine human music of 1977 and the intense, turbulent climate signals of 2010–2026 creates an unforgettable artistic and scientific experience.

6. What factors did our team consider?

- Data Authenticity: Every station and probe coordinate is mapped directly to real NASA SVS observation records (SVS #5313, #5153, #3912, #5669, #5196, #5011, #4960, #4950, #5533, #5147, #5148, #5154).

- Resilient Audio Fallbacks: In modern browsers that block autoplay or restrict SpeechSynthesis, our system automatically falls back to native Web Audio oscillators to prevent silence.

- Ergonomics: Adaptive controls ensure full touch and multi-gesture usability on compact mobile viewports without sacrificing the cinematic 3D space atmosphere on desktop.

THE RECEIVER Open-Source Codebase (GitHub): https://github.com/as777ms/voyager1
